names: 22nd Street Caltrain Station ADA Access Improvement
distance_note: The existing 22nd St Caltrain station (Pennsylvania Ave/Indiana St, Dogpatch) sits roughly 400-450m from both Pier 70's and Potrero Power Station's tracked boundaries -- grouped here under Pier 70 as the closer, better-established Dogpatch association.
summary: An accessibility retrofit of the existing, below-grade 22nd Street Caltrain station -- the only regular-service Caltrain station without wheelchair access. The project adds ramps to both platforms plus wayfinding and safety improvements. Design is under way (targeted complete summer 2027); construction is not slated to start until spring 2028, with completion targeted for mid-2029. Total project cost is $19,134,000, sponsored by the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain) with SFCTA (Prop L) and FTA funding.

milestones.text: Caltrain and SFCTA begin pursuing federal funding for the station's accessibility project.

SFCTA's Transportation Authority Board packet recommends $1,300,000 in Prop L funds for the project's design phase, part of a total funding plan of $19,134,000 (Planning/Conceptual Engineering $734,000 already spent via Prop K; Design Engineering $1,300,000 via Prop L; Construction $17,100,000, an engineer's estimate at 30% design).

SFCTA Board formally approves the $1,300,000 Prop L design-phase allocation (one of three projects sharing a combined $9.8M Prop L allocation that day, alongside the Powell St Improvement and the Mission Bay Ferry Landing).

The Federal Transit Administration's All Stations Accessibility Program awards the Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board $14.1 million for ADA improvements at the 22nd Street station -- matching almost exactly the funding gap SFCTA's own April 2026 plan had left as "Planned TBD".
Project completion targeted (station open for use expected spring 2029; full project completion targeted mid/late 2029).

facts.value: Peninsula Corridor Joint Powers Board (Caltrain), with funding from SFCTA (Prop L) and the FTA

One ramp on the northbound platform (about 305 ft long, 6.5% slope) and one on the southbound platform (about 465 ft long, 6.1% slope), plus tactile strips, lighting and signage. Platforms sit about 25 ft below street grade, currently reachable only by stairs.

open_questions: This record's placement under Pier 70 rather than Potrero Power Station reflects a roughly equal real-world distance (about 400-450m to each tracked boundary) plus the station's more established association with the Dogpatch/Pier 70 corridor in transit planning -- not a precise geometry test against a real station footprint (no Assessor parcel or site-plan figure exists to test against; see accuracy_caveat).

No construction start date is confirmed beyond the spring 2028 target implied by SFCTA's own milestone table; this could shift given design is only at an early stage as of this record's last_verified date.
